Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / PP1
Subject: General
Strand: My Family
Topic 2.1: Family members • father • mother • brothers • sisters • grandmothers • grandfathers
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 12

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Family members • father • mother • brothers • sisters • grandmothers • grandfathers, part of My Family in SNE  /  visual-impairment / PP1 General.

Key inquiry question: Why do we have family members at home?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Family members • father • mother • brothers • sisters • grandmothers • grandfathers together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Self-efficacy: learner develops confidence when identifying family members.

Communication and Collaboration: learner develops teamwork skills when role playing family members.

Values:
Patriotism: learner enhances citizenship when news talking about family members.

Peace: learner enhances harmonious relationship when role playing about family members.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Social cohesion: learner recites poems and sings songs about family members found at home.

Gender issues: learner enhances gender awareness when role playing about family members.

Link to other learning areas:

Family members relates to family members when learning about creation in Religious Activities.

12

Suggested Learning Resources

Charts, picture cards, tactile diagrams, models of family members, flashcards, photos, drawn pictures, glue, crayons, stickers, pencils, clay,

digital devices with assistive technology and plasticine, braille writing materials and equipment.
